rationale: Human Sjögren salivary flow was measured with a corn oil comparator. Rat gland flow and topical corn-derived lubrication give separate outcomes. The available Parkinson carrier report gives a composite and leaves clinical drooling severity under dietary refined corn oil unresolved.

The horse trial measured direct stride. The ENRGISE and Tessier trials measured human gait speed, and Xu measured functional mobility, with different directions across distinct outcomes. The Parkinson carrier report and mouse vehicle experiment do not establish a human stride effect attributable to dietary refined corn oil.

ENRGISE reports one serious fall in each of the corn-oil-only and fish-oil-only arms. Reports of composite mobility and animal slips leave habitual Parkinson fall frequency and an independent refined corn oil effect unresolved.

A Sjögren trial measured fatigue under a corn oil comparison but provides no clear group difference. The Japanese desk-work fatigue trial is complete with no public results located. The effect on Parkinson fatigue remains undetermined.

Canine feeding studies measured olfactory performance and supply no clear dietary maize-oil worsening. One crossover improved odor detection versus a distinct high-fat formulation. The human olfaction placebo contains an unverified ingredient and the mouse model used injected oil. The dietary refined corn oil effect in Parkinson disease remains open.
